children: U.S. jobless claims ticked down even further last week as the labor market continues to hold strong.

The number of people who filed for unemployment benefits was 197,000 in the week through Sept. 19, 1,000 lower than the revised 198,000 reported a week earlier, the Labor Department said Thursday. Economists surveyed by The Wall Street Journal were expecting to see the figure rise to 201,000.

Continuing claims, which scale with the total size of the unemployed population, totaled 1.72 million in the week through Sept. 12, climbing by 2,000 from the downwardly revised total a week earlier. The data on continuing claims lag the initial-claims data by a week.

After the Federal Reserve raised interest rates last week for the first time in years, Fed officials have been speculating that more cuts would likely be needed this year if inflation keeps running hot. The labor market's resilience has given the Fed few excuses not to raise rates while price growth remains above its 2% target.
